scope: legacy G1 1200 simulated seconds / 72000 fixed ticks population-memory stress

methodology.originalTest: tests/unit/battle.test.ts: runs 20 minutes of the combat system at hard population and memory bounds
methodology.temporaryChange: Only the frozen test timeout literal is changed from 20000ms to 60000ms. All 72000 iterations and every original assertion are retained.
methodology.sourceFreeze: All runtime src imports are captured by esbuild onLoad. Old uses git show 8364bf1:path; current uses file reads. SHA256 normalizes CRLF to LF. The module-preserving snapshots copy the same recorded imports without bundling.
methodology.isolation: Every process is sequential, maxWorkers=1, fileParallelism=false. Parent deferred browser simulation and long tests during this benchmark window.
methodology.measuredDuration: Vitest assertionResults.duration for the complete test body, including per-tick assertions; excludes process startup/import/transform time.

hotPathReview: GameSession is used only to create/start the seed-71 G1 initial state. The stress loop directly calls BattleDirector.beforeInput/afterInput; session.step, new endless director, upgrade projection and immune-cell simulation do not execute in this loop.
The loop has no endless state. New endless branches take their legacy path; the new simultaneous attack cap scan is guarded by s.endless and is skipped.

Existing planEnemySpacing evaluates pair overlaps plus up to five collision/energy candidates per moving overlapping body; moveEnemyThroughCrowd also checks live neighbors. These repeatedly visited crowd algorithms are byte-equivalent after line-ending normalization to 8364bf1.
No CPU sampling was performed. The hot-path notes are source inspection, not measured function-level percentages.

conclusion.result: No evidence of a material runtime regression in this legacy stress scenario. The original 20s wall-clock timeout has little headroom even for the old revision.
conclusion.rationale: Module-preserving current completes in about 18.74s versus old 18.65s (+0.45%). 30s provides about 60% headroom over this observed complete run without weakening simulation duration, population, memory or health assertions.
limits: The module-preserving comparison is one sequential pair, and bundled comparisons are three sequential pairs; these are diagnostics, not a statistical performance guarantee.
Host load, CPU scheduling and test-runner overhead can move wall time. The earlier parent-observed 21.176s timeout is not replayed or overwritten by this report.
This is a non-rendered post-failure G1 system stress host, not browser FPS, a successful player run, or endless-mode performance acceptance.
